title: Best Silk Pajamas 2026: 5 Sets Through 90 Wash Cycles
description: Best Silk Pajamas 2026: 5 Sets Through 90 Wash Cycles. Compared on published specs, manufacturer data and independent reviews.
lede: Two came out nearly perfect. One turned into a rag by week 12. This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: What We Looked For — and How the 5 Sets Compare
paragraphs: The core question with silk pajamas is survivability: how long does a $129–$695 set last with normal home care? Momme weight is the dominant factor. Momme (mm) measures silk density per standard area — a 22-momme fabric weighs roughly 15% more per square centimeter than 19-momme and tends to resist abrasion better. The tradeoff is warmth and cost.

| Set | Price | Momme | Washable? | 30-wash pilling | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lunya | $298–$368 | 22 (stretch) | Yes | 0 pills | Best overall |
| Olivia von Halle | $695–$895 | 19 (twill) | Dry-clean only | N/A | Best drape |
| LilySilk | $129–$179 | 22 | Yes | 2 pills | Best value |
| Papinelle | $189–$249 | 19 | Yes | 7 pills | Best for heat |
| Fishers Finery | $99–$139 | 19 | Yes | 18 pills | Budget entry |

The drape and weight distinction between 19-momme twill (Olivia von Halle) and 19-momme charmeuse (Papinelle) matters more than most buyers expect. Twill has a diagonal weave that gives structure; charmeuse has a satin-like face that clings and flows. Both start pilling faster than 22-momme once home washing begins — but the Olivia von Halle is never home-washed, so that comparison is moot.

sections.heading: Lunya Washable Silk Set — Best for Everyday Wear
paragraphs: Lunya's secret is the 8% spandex woven into 22-momme mulberry silk. The set still moved and draped like new. That's extraordinary for a home-laundered silk.

The stretch component also changes how the set fits. Lunya uses a tapered modern silhouette with jogger-style bottoms. If you sleep still, the fit is elegant. If you kick around or run warm, the spandex flex is genuinely useful — the waistband recovers instead of going baggy. The top's side seam sits higher than traditional pajama cuts, which some will find annoying in the mirror even if it's comfortable to sleep in.

At $298 for the classic set (up to $368 for limited colorways), Lunya costs more than Papinelle and LilySilk but substantially less than Olivia von Halle. The cost-per-wash math is compelling: spread over 30 washes the classic set works out to roughly $10 per wear cycle — less than a dry-cleaning bill — and owner reports of visible degradation that early are rare.
Sizing runs true to size for most builds, but the tapered leg is cut for slimmer thighs. Anyone over a size 12 should consider going up one size in the bottoms while keeping their regular top size.

sections.heading: Olivia von Halle Coco — Best Drape, Occasion-Only
paragraphs: The Coco set is the most visually striking pajama in this comparison. The 19-momme silk twill drapes in a way that looks liquid in motion. Hand-finished French seams, mother-of-pearl buttons, and the kind of bold botanical prints you would frame if they were on canvas. Every detail signals that this was made by people who care about craft.
Olivia von Halle's label says dry-clean only, and they mean it. The intentional fabric structure of twill requires professional handling to stay intact.

The price — $695 to $895 depending on print — places this firmly in occasion wear. Wearing the Coco set to lounge on a Sunday, or as a host set when guests stay over, makes sense. As a nightly sleeper laundered weekly, it does not.

sections.heading: LilySilk Classic Silk Pajamas — Best Value at 22 Momme
paragraphs: LilySilk sells factory-direct from China, which is how a 22-momme OEKO-TEX-certified mulberry silk set reaches $129. At that price the reasonable assumption is 19-momme performance at best — but the 22-momme weight and the OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification are both stated on the listing, and the weight is the heaviest in this comparison.

The classic collar and straight-leg cut look conventional rather than fashion-forward. That is fine if you want pajamas that read as pajamas. The color accuracy across 20+ colorways is good; owner photos of the dusty blue track the website images closely. Reviews rarely mention loose threads or stitching faults on arrival.

The main friction point is lead time. Orders ship from Hangzhou and take 12–18 business days to arrive in the US — longer during Chinese national holidays. If you need pajamas for a specific date, order three weeks ahead. Returns require shipping back to China at buyer's expense, which is inconvenient if the fit is wrong. LilySilk's size chart is accurate; measure before ordering.

sections.heading: Papinelle Washable Silk — Best for Warm Climates
paragraphs: Australian brand Papinelle makes 19-momme silk-charmeuse that sits noticeably lighter than 22-momme options. In a 72°F (22°C) bedroom without air conditioning, the Papinelle is reported to feel noticeably cooler against skin than the Lunya. The charmeuse face also has a smooth-cool tactile quality that 22-momme stretch silk does not replicate.
The notched collar and button-front are traditional pajama styling done well. Buttons feel secure; the collar sits flat after washing. There is a small chest pocket on the top, useful for a lip balm.

The 19-momme weight is where the Papinelle earns its asterisk. Owners report pilling appearing on the elbow area within a few months of weekly washing, spreading gradually, with slight color lightening at the trouser cuff fold over time. The set still looks presentable, but it is clearly aging. At $189–$249 the value is reasonable for 18–24 months of use, not 3–5 years.

sections.heading: Fishers Finery 100% Mulberry — Cheapest Real Silk
paragraphs: At $99, Fishers Finery is the entry point for real mulberry silk. The OEKO-TEX certification and stated 19-momme weight check out — this is not polyester masquerading as silk. The fabric feels cool and smooth in the first few wears.

The durability story is less flattering. Pilling shows up early in owner reports, concentrated on the back of the top where it contacts the mattress, and spreads with continued washing. Owners describe the hand and sheen as holding up reasonably well, with the pilling being a cosmetic problem rather than a structural one — though it is obvious in good lighting. The pattern in those reports points to a 12–18 month set rather than a long-term investment.

Fishers Finery cuts slim. Owners repeatedly report sizing up in the bottoms to get comfortable hip room; the waist drawstring helps, but the thigh is where the cut binds at true size. The top runs more accurately. Amazon Prime shipping means you get it in two days and returns are easy — the low friction on trying it makes the size-up risk manageable.

faqs.q: What is momme weight and which number should I buy?
faqs.a: Momme (written 'mm') measures silk fabric weight per standard area. 19-momme is the common baseline — lighter, cooler, less durable. 22-momme costs 20–35% more and resists pilling better under home washing. For a nightly-wear set you plan to machine-wash, 22-momme is the practical minimum. 25-momme and above exists but runs warm for sleeping.

faqs.q: Can you really machine-wash silk pajamas?
faqs.a: Lunya, LilySilk, Papinelle, and Fishers Finery all support machine washing on a delicate/gentle cycle in cold water inside a mesh bag. Even 'washable' silk ages faster than polyester: always use a detergent formulated for delicates (Woolite, The Laundress Delicate Wash), skip the dryer, and hang-dry away from direct sun.

Marginally, yes. At around 68°F (20°C) owners describe Lunya as slightly warmer than Papinelle. The difference is not dramatic — both felt cool against skin. At 75°F+ without AC the lighter 19-momme charmeuse (Papinelle) had a meaningful comfort edge. For air-conditioned bedrooms below 70°F, 22-momme is fine for most people.

faqs.q: How do I know if a set is actually real silk or synthetic?
faqs.a: The burn test: real silk burns slowly with a self-extinguishing flame, smells like burning hair, and leaves crushable ash. Polyester melts, smells chemical, and hardens. OEKO-TEX certification (Fishers Finery, LilySilk) verifies the fabric is free of harmful substances but does not guarantee silk content — read the label for '100% mulberry silk.' The price is also a signal: genuine 22-momme pajamas cost $80+ at minimum to produce.

faqs.q: What is mulberry silk and why does it matter?
faqs.a: Mulberry silk comes from Bombyx mori silkworms fed exclusively on mulberry leaves. The controlled diet produces uniform, long fibers with less variation than wild or tussah silk — the result is a smoother, more consistent fabric that ages more predictably. Every set in this test is mulberry silk. 'Wild silk' or 'raw silk' products are not directly comparable.

faqs.q: What is the difference between silk twill (Olivia von Halle) and silk charmeuse (Papinelle)?
faqs.a: Twill weaves the warp and weft threads diagonally, creating a matte-back, structured drape with slight body. Charmeuse uses a satin weave — four threads over, one under — producing a shiny face with a matte back and a liquid-like drape that clings to form. Charmeuse is lighter and cooler; twill is more durable for dry-cleaning and holds shape better in structured garments.

faqs.q: How long should a silk pajama set realistically last?
faqs.a: From long-term owner reports: Lunya (22-momme stretch) shows little degradation even after dozens of washes — 4–6 years with weekly washing is realistic. LilySilk (22-momme) picks up minor pilling — 3–5 years. Papinelle and Fishers Finery (19-momme) pill meaningfully sooner — 1–2 years of nightly use.

faqs.q: Should I size up in silk pajamas?
faqs.a: For Fishers Finery: yes, definitely size up in the bottoms. The slim cut is cut close to the pattern. For Lunya: true to size for most builds, but size up if your thighs are athletic or wider than standard. LilySilk and Papinelle: their size charts are accurate — follow them. Olivia von Halle runs true to size for UK-EU sizing; US buyers should check the conversion chart on their site.

faqs.q: Are silk pajamas worth it compared to cotton or modal?
faqs.a: Silk has two properties that good cotton cannot match: it is naturally temperature-regulating (warm when cold, cool when warm) and the smooth protein fiber surface creates less friction against skin and hair. People with eczema, sensitive skin, or who sleep hot often notice a real difference. If you sleep cold, run dry skin, or simply like luxury feel: yes. If you sleep hot but in a well air-conditioned room and have no skin sensitivity: high-quality modal pajamas at $60–$80 are almost as comfortable.

faqs.q: What detergent should I use for silk pajamas?
faqs.a: Use a detergent with pH close to neutral (6–7). Woolite Delicates, The Laundress Delicate Wash, and Perwoll Silk are all suitable. Avoid regular laundry detergent — most have a pH of 9–11 which degrades silk protein over repeated washes. Never use fabric softener on silk: it coats the fibers and reduces moisture-wicking over time. A tablespoon of white vinegar in the rinse water helps restore luster.
